title: VOROM-X — Reduced-Order Aerodynamic Solver
impact: Developed a Python research framework for wing loading, induced drag and configuration trade studies; applied it to a blended-wing-body design study.
summary: High-efficiency, object-oriented 3D potential flow research tool for preliminary aircraft aerodynamic design, planform optimization (sweep, dihedral, twist/washout), and flight-physics trade studies.
problem: Early-stage aircraft configuration trades require rapid evaluation of induced drag, spanwise circulation, and stability derivatives without the prohibitive computational cost of 3D RANS.
approach: Developed a 3D horseshoe vortex lattice solver with Trefftz-plane momentum-deficit integration for rigorous induced drag estimation, coupled with automated stability analysis.
methods: Biot-Savart induction kernel; Trefftz-plane wake integration; automated sweep and washout parametric trade studies; longitudinal trim and static margin computation; comprehensive unit testing.
validation: Compared aerodynamic trends with published experimental data and XFLR5. Agreement depends on the operating condition; high-incidence drag and nonlinear coupled convergence remain important model limitations.
results: Explored sweep and washout trades in a tailless blended-wing-body study, including a 20° sweep / −3° washout configuration. This is a research application, not flight validation.
learnings: Deep theoretical and numerical mastery of potential flow methods, wake roll-up limits, and automated flight-physics derivation in scientific Python.
next_steps: Integration of unsteady vortex lattice method (UVLM) and aeroelastic beam coupling.

title: High-Lift Aerodynamics — Transition-SST RANS & XFOIL
impact: Compared transition-sensitive RANS and XFOIL predictions for the HLHLSD4 airfoil at Re = 1 million; assessed separation behaviour and mesh sensitivity.
summary: A joint numerical fluid mechanics project at ISAE-SUPAERO investigating high-lift airfoil behaviour through RANS CFD and XFOIL.
problem: Predicting the stall boundary and maximum lift coefficient of high-lift sections requires resolving both natural/bypass boundary-layer transition and separation bubbles.
approach: Compared Transition-SST RANS solutions with XFOIL, examining pressure, skin friction and separation across operating conditions.
methods: Built structured multi-block C-grids with near-wall refinement (y⁺ < 1); executed grid sensitivity analysis across three mesh densities; extracted computed suction-side pressure distributions and skin friction coefficient profiles.
validation: At 10° incidence, the reported medium-to-fine differences were approximately 0.15% in lift and 2% in drag. These are mesh-sensitivity results, not experimental accuracy; an asymptotic convergence regime was not strictly established.
results: Examined separation and its upstream migration with increasing incidence. Used pressure and skin-friction distributions to investigate differences between the modelling approaches.
learnings: Transition-sensitive modelling, structured boundary-layer meshing and interpretation of model disagreement.
next_steps: 3D swept wing and multi-element flap configuration analysis.

title: ApexSim — CFD Workflow & Vehicle Performance
impact: Developed a Python workflow connecting aerodynamic maps, automated CFD studies and vehicle-performance exploration.
summary: An automated engineering methods framework designed to streamline high-throughput CFD parameter sweeps, enforce numerical verification gates, and generate continuous aerodynamic databases.
problem: Manual CFD execution is prone to human error, lack of mesh convergence tracking, and unverified boundary condition sensitivities during large design of experiments (DOE).
approach: Developed automated execution scripts that interface with open-source RANS solvers (SU2), parse residuals, enforce convergence thresholds, and train surrogate models on validated datasets.
methods: CFD workflow automation, domain-sensitivity assessment, force-stationarity checks, and polynomial ridge / RBF surrogate modelling.
validation: The project record describes regression checks and domain-sensitivity gates. These are numerical workflow checks, not correlation with race-track measurements.
results: Established a workflow for investigating domain sensitivity before accepting aerodynamic maps for downstream studies.
learnings: Numerical verification, reproducible CFD automation and the limitations of surrogate models.
next_steps: Active subspace dimension reduction for high-dimensional design spaces.

title: TRACE FanGEO — Fan Geometry to BFM Preprocessing
impact: Developing a requirement-driven chain from fan duty and throughflow to blade geometry, surface normals and metal-blockage fields.
summary: Current master’s thesis at ISAE-SUPAERO, DAEP: Requirement-Driven Fan Geometry to Body Force Model Preprocessing.
problem: Bridging the gap between 1D thermodynamic cycle requirements and 3D aerodynamic blade geometry is traditionally iterative, manual, and prone to CAD interface inconsistencies.
approach: Implemented a semi-analytical throughflow solver based on radial equilibrium and spanwise work distribution Δ(rCθ), coupled to parametric B-spline blade generation.
methods: Radial equilibrium integration; velocity triangle closure; flow-to-metal angle deviation modeling; automated stagger, camber, and thickness distribution across 41 spanwise sections; interface consistency verification.
validation: Geometric and numerical checks examine reconstruction, surface derivatives, normals and interface consistency. Full downstream CFD and experimental fan validation are separate stages.
results: Connected throughflow and geometry generation while identifying chord/stagger interface inconsistencies. Outputs support downstream body-force modelling; they do not establish a fully validated fan design.
learnings: Deep understanding of turbomachinery gas dynamics, throughflow methods, and automated geometric parameterisation.
next_steps: Gated downstream solver coupling and validation.

title: Structural Test Engineering & Hardware Design for eVTOL
role: Mechanical Design Engineer Intern @ Lilium eAircraft
impact: Defined structural test requirements and designed custom test fixtures and support hardware for composite sandwich panels in Siemens NX with ASME Y14.5 GD&T; executed pre-test nonlinear FEA in ANSYS.
summary: Professional aerospace engineering internship within Lilium's mechanical testing division, developing custom test fixtures, planning test matrices, and running pre-test structural simulations.
problem: Ensuring structural integrity and predictable load transfer across composite sandwich panels and insert joints under severe operational and certification flight loads.
approach: Combined detailed fixture design in Siemens NX with pre-test nonlinear finite element analysis to ensure proper boundary condition replication on test benches.
methods: CAD modeling and drawing preparation under ASME Y14.5 GD&T; nonlinear pre-test FEM in ANSYS Workbench to predict stress concentrations and fixture deflection; configuration management in Teamcenter.
validation: Interface fit checks and stiffness verification against physical test bench interfaces.
results: Delivered fully documented fixture packages and test requirement matrices, supporting reliable structural characterization of composite joints.
learnings: Industrial aerospace engineering standards, PDM release workflows, GD&T application, and physical testing interfaces.
next_steps: Dynamic fatigue test correlation and environmental degradation testing.

title: Fixed-Wing UAV Aerodynamics & Prototype Flight Testing
impact: Conducted low-Reynolds aerodynamic and stability analysis for an ~2 m fixed-wing UAV using XFLR5 and Fluent; designed 3D airframe geometry in SolidWorks and supported prototype flight testing.
summary: Aerospace design internship focusing on aerodynamic optimization, configuration layout, and flight-test support for a medium-scale fixed-wing autonomous aircraft.
problem: Optimizing the cruise efficiency, stall behavior, and longitudinal stability of an unmanned aircraft operating in the low-Reynolds-number regime.
approach: Iterative aerodynamic design using panel codes and RANS CFD, followed by 3D CAD packaging and prototype flight-test support.
methods: Low-Re airfoil selection and polar calculation in XFLR5; 3D wing-body RANS simulation in ANSYS Fluent; 3D surface modeling and structural packaging in SolidWorks.
validation: Aerodynamic analysis and prototype flight-test support formed complementary parts of the internship; no quantified simulation-to-flight correlation is claimed.
results: Contributed aerodynamic analysis and airframe CAD to prototype development.
learnings: Hands-on experience in fixed-wing aircraft design synthesis, low-Re aerodynamic physics, and rapid flight-test iteration.
next_steps: Automated flight data acquisition and onboard telemetry synchronization.

title: Aerodynamics of Passenger Aircraft with Distributed Electric Propulsion (DEP)
impact: Investigated aerodynamic interaction between a transport-aircraft wing and simplified stationary nacelle installations using steady RANS within a 4-engineer team.
summary: Undergraduate honours thesis investigating the aerodynamic trade-offs and surface flow fields of a transport-aircraft wing integrated with distributed propulsor nacelles.
problem: Integrating multiple propulsors along the wing span alters the local pressure field and boundary-layer development, impacting clean-wing cruise efficiency.
approach: Modeled baseline and nacelle-installed transport wing geometries to systematically map pressure gradients, velocity profiles, and regional lift-to-drag trade-offs.
methods: Clean-wing and installed CAD generation in SolidWorks; high-density volume meshing in HyperMesh; steady-state RANS simulations in ANSYS Fluent; post-processing of boundary-layer velocity slices.
validation: Compared clean-wing and stationary-nacelle configurations within a four-person capstone study. The work does not represent powered propeller slipstream validation.
results: Examined local pressure and velocity fields around stationary nacelle installations and their influence on the wing boundary layer. Rotating propellers were outside the model scope.
learnings: Foundational grounding in 3D CFD meshing, boundary-layer physics, and propulsion-airframe integration fundamentals.
next_steps: Full actuator disk or rotating propeller CFD modeling to capture slipstream swirl.

title: Cryogenic Propellant Tank Structural FEA & Buckling Analysis
role: Mechanical / Structural Team Member @ WARR Rocketry TUM
impact: Analyzed structural performance and buckling margins of a CFRP cryogenic propellant tank for student sounding rockets under combined pressure and axial launch loads.
summary: Structural finite element analysis and laminate optimization for lightweight carbon-fiber cryogenic propellant tanks operating under extreme pressure and thermal gradients.
problem: Cryogenic composite tanks face high internal pressures and risk thin-wall buckling under launch acceleration and bending moments.
approach: Contributed finite element modelling and structural assessment within a student rocketry team.
methods: Composite structural finite element analysis and buckling assessment.
validation: Student-team analytical and numerical structural assessment; no flight qualification or certified structural margin is claimed.
results: Investigated structural behaviour and potential buckling modes to support student design work.
learnings: Composite laminate analysis, cryogenic pressure vessel behavior, and structural buckling assessment.
next_steps: Progressive failure analysis and manufacturing defect sensitivity.

title: Subsurface Defect Mapping Using GPR
impact: Used ground-penetrating radar and signal processing in a non-destructive testing practical to investigate subsurface features.
summary: Executed non-destructive inspection of concrete structures to map subsurface defects, calibrating dielectric properties and generating B- and C-scan profiles.
problem: Detecting internal flaws in thick structures without destructive access.
approach: Use GPR for high-frequency electromagnetic wave reflection analysis.
methods: Radar data acquisition and processing in RADAN 7.
validation: Verification of defect size and depth using Time-of-Flight (TOF) and permittivity calculations.
results: Interpreted radar profiles to identify subsurface features and discuss measurement limitations.
learnings: Experience with GPR hardware and signal processing software; understanding of wave propagation in dielectric media.
next_steps: Integration of automated robotic scanning for larger surfaces.

title: Optimized Additive Manufacturing: RC Transport Vehicle
impact: Designed and prototyped a 3D-printed RC transport vehicle in an additive manufacturing practical.
summary: High-performance functional prototyping focusing on weight optimization and load-bearing capacity using FDM printing.
problem: Carry a 500g payload on a lightweight 3D-printed chassis.
approach: Topology optimization and functional integration of wheels and chassis.
methods: NX-based design; material property testing; iterative prototyping.
results: Built and evaluated a functional prototype as part of a student design exercise.
learnings: Design for Additive Manufacturing (DfAM); load-path optimization.
next_steps: Integration of sensors for autonomous navigation.

title: Spacecraft Power Subsystem Architecture
impact: Architected the end-to-end power system for a LEO debris-tracking satellite, including orbital energy balance and hardware sizing.
summary: Designed generation, storage, and distribution systems for an AI-based LEO mission, selecting mission-critical hardware and performing energy balance modeling.
problem: Ensure continuous power supply for high-demand AI processing on a limited LEO cube-sat platform.
approach: System-level modeling of generation vs consumption throughout the orbital cycle.
methods: Orbital mechanics for solar flux calculation; component selection (EaglePicher batteries, Sparkwing arrays).
validation: Worse-case scenario analysis (eclipse duration, peak load).
results: Developed solar-array and battery sizing estimates for an academic spacecraft power budget. This was a conceptual design study, not flight-hardware delivery.
learnings: Space hardware standards and orbital energy budget workflows.
next_steps: Integration of thermal management constraints into the power model.

title: Baja SAE ATV Design & Integration
impact: Contributed to chassis, suspension and vehicle assembly in a student off-road engineering project.
summary: Designed and fabricated core subsystems for a high-performance off-road vehicle, focusing on structural integrity and suspension geometry.
problem: Develop a lightweight yet durable chassis for extreme off-road competition.
approach: Iterative design focusing on occupant safety and vehicle dynamics.
methods: Chassis modeling; suspension kinematics optimization; manual jig assembly and welding support.
validation: Student design and assembly work; no formal vehicle qualification is claimed.
results: Supported integration of mechanical subsystems into the student vehicle.
learnings: Practical manufacturing skills; suspension geometry; team-based engineering.
next_steps: Weight reduction through carbon-fiber body panels.
